findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies math.floor to a datetime key
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. Its `get_item_key` copies the integer `Paginator` logic and calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`. That raises `TypeError` for a datetime object, so any non-empty page served through the optimized path returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` has the same mismatch: it returns the raw integer cursor value, which is then compared against the datetime column in the WHERE clause, giving wrong results or a DB error. This class needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion, for example by subclassing it.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are sliced directly into the Django queryset
findings.body: With `enable_advanced_features`, a negative `cursor.offset` taken from the user-supplied cursor string is used as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise an error, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-10:0` causes a 500 instead of a `BadPaginationError`. The comments say this is meant to 'access data beyond normal pagination bounds'. That is the wrong goal for a pagination primitive, and the claim that permissions are checked at the queryset level does not justify it. Negative offsets should be rejected, as `OffsetPaginator` already does.

findings.title: BasePaginator still passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only next cursors. A prev cursor with a negative offset from user input still reaches the queryset slice and raises an unhandled error, giving a 500. Meanwhile the clamping on next cursors silently hides invalid input. All paginators built on `BasePaginator` are affected. Negative offsets should raise `BadPaginationError` consistently.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated for every non-superuser request, even when `optimized_pagination` was not requested. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be None, for example for staff or token-based access that passes `OrganizationAuditPermission` without a membership. In that case the whole audit log endpoint fails with a 500. The member check should be guarded and evaluated only when `use_optimized` is true.

findings.title: Switching segment keys from sets to sorted sets breaks on keys left by the old code
findings.body: Segment keys `span-buf:s:*` are now written with ZADD and read with ZCARD/ZSCAN. During a deploy, keys created by the old code are still Redis SETs and live up to `redis_ttl` (one hour). ZADD/ZCARD on those keys raises WRONGTYPE, which fails the whole pipeline in `process_spans`. ZSCAN in `_load_segment_data` fails the same way, crashing the consumer and flusher. A migration step, new key prefix, or type-tolerant handling is needed.

findings.title: Spans are evicted silently with a hardcoded limit and no metric
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, `zpopmin` drops the spans with the earliest end timestamps, and nothing records it. The old code emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged an error. The limit is hardcoded in Lua, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still accepted but no longer used, which is misleading configuration. The data loss is now invisible to operators. The limit should be passed in as an argument, and the eviction count returned so it can be reported as a metric.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000 and the caveat comment removed
findings.body: The redirect-following loop now stops after 1000 hops, and the comment explaining that deeper trees will not be joined correctly was removed. Segments with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now be split into separate segments without any indication. The PR does not explain this behaviour change.

findings.title: New span eviction logic has no tests
findings.body: The PR adds eviction of the oldest spans when a segment exceeds 1000, but no test covers it. Nothing checks which spans are kept, that the count is capped correctly when sets are merged through `zunionstore`, or that the root span survives eviction. The removed `max_segment_spans` behaviour also had no replacement test.
